 A chatbot (Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot) predicts helpful words based on patterns in huge amounts of text.

 It is not a search engine you can trust blindly. It can sound sure and still be wrong. This is called a “hallucination.”

 Open your web browser (Chrome, Safari or Edge). Click the address bar at the top, type gemini.google.com and press Enter.

 Read the answer. AI can be wrong, so check at least one fact

 Short lesson ideas for PreK-5th, 6th-8th and 9th-12th teachers and for parents. Each one is free and safe. Never type student names, grades or health details into a chatbot.

t: AI-Smart Lessons & Free Websites — 🧸 PreK-5th: What is AI?
x:
Sort like a computer (20 min). Give pairs 12 animal picture cards. They invent a rule ("has stripes") and sort. Say: AI learns rules from lots of examples, and it can guess wrong.
 Draw for the computer. Play Quick, Draw! on the big screen. Ask: how did it guess? When did it get it wrong?
 Translate a note home. Prompt: “Rewrite this class note in [language] at a simple reading level. Keep dates and times exact.” Have a speaker check it if you can.
 Adapt for ELL and IEP. Prompt: “Make 3 versions of this task: with pictures, with shorter steps, and as a read-aloud script. Grade [ ].” No names or diagnoses.

t: AI-Smart Lessons & Free Websites — 🧪 6th-8th: Spot fakes and use AI honestly
x:
Spot the fake (40 min). Show 4 posts (2 real, 2 AI-made). Teach 3 questions: Who made it? What's the proof? Who else says so? Exit ticket: judge one new post.
 Class AI agreement. Prompt: “Write a one-page class agreement for grade [ ] about when AI is a helper (ideas, feedback) and when it is cheating (handing in its words). Use kid-friendly words.”
 Train a simple AI. In Teachable Machine students record 2 objects, test, then try to fool it. Discuss: why did it make mistakes? (Bias from too few examples.)

t: AI-Smart Lessons & Free Websites — 🎓 9th-12th: Check facts, give fair feedback, explore careers
x:
Fact-check the chatbot (45 min). Students ask a chatbot 5 questions on the unit, then check each claim against 2 real sources and cite them. Score: claims that held up.
 Fair essay feedback. Prompt: “Using this rubric, give 3 strengths and 3 next steps for this essay. Don't give a grade.” Remove the name first; you edit and you grade.
 Career interview. Prompt: “Pretend you're a [job]. A student will interview you; answer in plain words.” Then verify pay and training on the Occupational Outlook Handbook .

t: AI-Smart Lessons & Free Websites — 👪 Parents: fakes, translation and screen time
x:
Talk about fakes. Look at one viral post together and ask the 3 questions. Remind your child: voices and videos can be faked too.
 Translate school notes. Prompt: “Translate this school note into [language]. Keep dates, times and names of places exact.” Then double-check the dates.
 Set screen-time limits. Use Google Family Link (Android) or Apple Screen Time (in iPhone Settings). Agree on the limit together.
